candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection-prevention interventions and perioperative safety
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — S. aureus decolonization
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the purpose and limits of targeted S. aureus nasal decolonization in high-risk surgical care.

options.A: The protocol reduces S. aureus carriage at common body sites and is used to lower infection risk in selected high-risk settings; it does not replace standard infection-prevention measures
options.B: The protocol cures any bloodstream or deep surgical infection that may already be present without systemic treatment
options.C: Every person colonized with MRSA should receive mupirocin indefinitely regardless of clinical setting or resistance concerns
options.D: Once decolonization is started, hand hygiene and other perioperative infection-control practices are no longer necessary

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends targeted S. aureus decolonization/pathogen-reduction strategies in selected high-risk settings, including certain surgical populations. Intranasal mupirocin or another nasal antistaphylococcal agent is commonly paired with chlorhexidine cleansing to reduce carriage and infection risk. It is not universal indefinite therapy, does not treat established invasive infection by itself, and does not replace core infection-control practices.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Targeted nasal decolonization can reduce S. aureus carriage/infection risk in selected high-risk surgical settings but is not universal or a substitute for infection-control practices.
candidate.source_document_title: Strategies to Prevent Hospital-onset Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infections in Acute Care Facilities
candidate.source_locator: Section 2 — high-risk surgeries: intranasal antistaphylococcal antibiotic/antiseptic such as mupirocin or iodophor plus chlorhexidine wash/wipes; core infection-control measures remain required
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.stem: A client known to carry S. aureus in the nares is scheduled for a high-risk orthopedic procedure and has a facility protocol for intranasal mupirocin plus chlorhexidine skin cleansing before surgery. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?
